author: BBC News
description:
A manhunt is under way in the German capital after a car was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event, police say.

The mayor of Berlin, Kai Wegner, has called the incident, "an attack on our free and open-minded society".

Police in Berlin say one person is dead and 16 others are injured, with some sustaining life-threatening injuries.

author: BBC News
description:
Around 270,000 people in France and Spain have been forced to flee their homes to escape fires which have been raging for days, as winds and high temperatures hamper efforts to contain them. 

In France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated in south-western regions of Gironde and Landes regions. The country has mobilised its military to help with the response and extra reinforcements from the army have been sent to help firefighters by clearing brush and creating fire breaks.

French President Emmanuel Macron held an emergency meeting with ministers as around 30 separate major fires rage - a situation which the government said was unprecedented.

In Spain, where a state of emergency has been declared, wildfires have been threatening the capital, Madrid. Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez admitted there are "complex times ahead". 

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Joe Inwood.

author: BBC News
description:
Touching, embracing and kissing before stressful events may be an ancient way of building trust, according to scientists studying the behaviour of our closest ape relatives.
 
Researchers at Durham University, England, studied chimpanzees and bonobos using physical contact to reassure each other ahead of conflicts over food.
 
One of the most surprising findings was that chimpanzees, despite their reputation for aggression, engaged in close contact, including placing fingers in one another's mouths.

author: BBC News
description:
India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned after weeks of protests over exam paper leaks and testing irregularities.
 
The demonstrations were spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) - not a real party, but a satirical campaign turned national movement.

What began as a student-led campaign against alleged exam paper leaks became one of India's biggest displays of public dissent in recent years, with thousands camping in Delhi and demonstrations spreading across the country.

author: BBC News
description:
Firefighters are struggling to contain wildfires raging across Europe.

An evacuation alert for residents in the south-west of France takes the number of people displaced to more than 220,000.

In Spain, about 25,000 were told to evacuate as a local official says that containing wildfires near Madrid is "beyond the capacity" of firefighters.

A major incident has also been declared by Police Scotland, as emergency services continue to tackle a wildfire which has been burning in the Cairngorms National Park for 10 days.
